summary: The selected replay pushes a boulder from the hero-adjacent square into a pit. C removes it from the source square, lets flooreffects consume it in the pit, then returns 0 so the hero can advance. JavaScript stops at moverock_core’s blanket trap-effect refusal. Source review shows the full task must port moverock_core and its return-valued cannot_push helper, whose branches handle giant pickup/step-over and squeeze results for blocked-push callers.

source.branch: moverock_core spans source lines 348-638 and includes boulder visibility/pile ordering, movement prerequisites, return-valued cannot_push failure routes, and destination trap/liquid effects. The selected PIT/SPIKED_PIT branch extracts the boulder, temporarily marks the destination visible, calls flooreffects(otmp, rx, ry, "fall"), replaces it if the effect did not consume it, redraws a visible monster, and returns whether another boulder remains at the source. cannot_push spans lines 262-312: giants may pick up or step over the boulder depending on inventory/pickup/Sokoban state, riding skill changes feedback, and a small/light hero may squeeze into the square; these branches can change state and print messages.

hack.c:moverock_core is the only active caller of cannot_push. Its five call sites at lines 430, 447, 482, 487, and 634 cover too-small heroes, diagonal Sokoban refusal, a blocking corporeal monster, a closed destination door, and an invalid destination. Each returns cannot_push’s result unchanged.
dependencies: The natural trap route depends on do.c:flooreffects(otmp, rx, ry, "fall") and its existing pit behavior, which consumes the boulder and prints the pit-fill message.

The source-complete moverock_core port must preserve existing dependencies and return use, including trap-effect helpers, boulder_hits_pool(), dopush(), cannot_push_msg(), and its active caller test_move(..., DO_MOVE). Do not replace a consumed return with a guessed value.

cannot_push is impure: the giant branch may invoke autopick_testobj and sokoban_guilt, its branches print messages, and its return value controls whether the hero steps into the boulder square. A recorded failure-path recipe is required in addition to the selected successful pit-fill route.
